extracted.intended_audience: NDA/ANDA/505(b)(2) applicants and pharmaceutical regulatory affairs professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements in 21 CFR Part 314 covering (a) submission and content of patent information for NDAs (including method-of-use patents), (b) procedures for 505(b)(2) applications, pediatric use data requirements, ACNU applications for nonprescription drugs, and (c) amendment timing rules. Focused on how to prepare, submit, correct, and disclose required materials and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-of-use patent submission — statement whether patent claims approved methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the patent claims one or more approved methods of using the approved drug product and a description of each approved method of use and related patent claim of the patent being submitted;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required as part of patent information submitted for a patent that claims methods of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify labeling sections referencing claimed method-of-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the specific section(s) and subsection(s) of the approved labeling for the drug product that describes the method of use claimed by the patent submitted;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the exact labeling locations so readers can find the approved method of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishable description of patented method-of-use
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the patented method of use as required for publication, which must contain adequate information to assist 505(b)(2) and ANDA applicants in determining whether a listed method-of-use patent claims a use for which the 505(b)(2) or ANDA applicant is not seeking approval (for example, if the method(s) of use claimed by the patent does not cover an indication or other approved condition of use in its entirety, then the applicant must describe only the specific approved method of use claimed by the patent for which a claim of patent infringement could reasonably be asserted if a person not licensed by the owner of the patent engaged in the manufacture, use, or sale of the drug product);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must be sufficiently specific to enable potential applicants to assess overlap—if patent only partially covers an approved indication, describe the specific claimed approved method that could give rise to infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement whether method-of-use patent also claims substance/product
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant that submits information for a patent that claims one or more methods of using the drug product must also submit information described in either paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(N) or (O) of this section, regarding whether that patent also claims either the drug substance (active ingredient) or the drug product (composition/formulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a method-of-use patent, disclose whether the patent additionally claims the active ingredient or composition/formulation using the referenced subparagraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of no relevant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are no relevant patents that claim the approved drug substance (active ingredient), the approved drug product (formulation or composition), or approved method(s) of use and with respect to which a claim of patent infringement could reasonably be asserted if a person not licensed by the owner of the patent engaged in the manufacture, use, or sale of the drug product;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no such patents exist, applicant must make the appropriate verification (see Form FDA 3542/3542a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed verification statement for patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed verification that states: The undersigned declares that this is an accurate and complete submission of patent information for the NDA, amendment, or supplement approved under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. This time-sensitive patent information or response to a request under 21 CFR 314.53(f)(1) is submitted pursuant to 21 CFR 314.53. I attest that I am familiar with 21 CFR 314.53 and this submission complies with the requirements of the regulation. I verify under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attestation must accompany submitted patent information and is a legal verification under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and signature information on patent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on whether the applicant, patent owner or attorney, agent, representative, or other authorized official signed the form; the name of the person; and the full address, phone number and, if available, the fax number and email address;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full contact details and identify the person who signed the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to required patent information submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to required submission of patent information: (1) If an applicant submits the information described in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(N) for a patent that claims the drug substance (active ingredient) and meets the requirements for listing on that basis, then the applicant is not required to provide the information described in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(O) of this section on whether that patent also claims the drug product (composition/formulation). (2) If an applicant submits the information described in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(O) for a patent that claims the drug product (composition/formulation) and meets the requirements for listing on that basis, then the applicant is not required to provide the information described in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(N) of this section on whether that patent also claims the drug substance (active ingredient). (3) If the applicant submits a supplement for a change other than one of the changes listed under paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section, then the patent information submission requirements of paragraph (d)(2)(ii) of this section apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies limited circumstances where redundant information is not required and references supplement-related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification procedure when there are no relevant patents (Form use)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant believes that there are no relevant patents that claim the drug substance (active ingredient), drug product (formulation or composition), or the method(s) of use for which the applicant has received approval, and with respect to which a claim of patent infringement could reasonably be asserted if a person not licensed by the owner of the patent engaged in the manufacture, use, or sale of the drug product, the applicant will verify this information in the appropriate form, Form FDA 3542 or 3542a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form FDA 3542 or 3542a to verify 'no relevant patents' assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized signature requirement for declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The declarations required by this section must be signed by the applicant or patent owner, or the applicant's or patent owner's attorney, agent (representative), or other authorized official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatory may be applicant, patent owner, or authorized representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — submit patent information with original NDA and for patents issued before NDA
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must submit with its original NDA submitted under this part, the information described in paragraph (c) of this section on each drug substance (active ingredient), drug product (formulation and composition), and method-of-use patent issued before the NDA is filed with FDA and for which patent information is required to be submitted under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents issued before NDA filing must be included in the original NDA submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — submit patent information within 30 days for patents issued after filing but before approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is issued after the NDA is filed with FDA but before the NDA is approved, the applicant must, within 30 days of the date of issuance of the patent, submit the required patent information in an amendment to the NDA under § 314.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly issued patents during pendency before approval trigger a 30-day amendment requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information submission required for certain supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must submit patent information required under paragraph (c) of this section for a patent that claims the drug substance, drug product, or method of use for which approval is sought in any of the following supplements: (A) To add or change the dosage form or route of administration; (B) To add or change the strength; or (C) To change the drug product from prescription use to over-the-counter use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these specific supplement types, include patent info claiming the changed attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information rules for supplements involving other changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant submits a supplement for a change other than one of the changes listed under paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section (for example, to change the formulation, to add a new indication or other condition of use, or to make any other patented change regarding the drug substance, drug product, or any method of use), then: (A) If existing patents already submitted claim the changed product, the applicant is not required to resubmit unless the published description would change; (B) If existing patents no longer claim the changed product, applicant must submit request to remove that patent information at time of approval of the supplement; (C) If one or more existing patents claim the changed product and such patent information has not been submitted, applicant must submit the patent information required under paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when to resubmit, withdraw, or newly submit patent information for supplements that change the product in other ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newly issued patents after NDA approval — 30-day submission and consequences for untimely filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is issued for a drug substance, drug product, or method of use after an NDA is approved, the applicant must submit to FDA the required patent information within 30 days of the date of issuance of the patent. If the required patent information is not submitted within 30 days of the issuance of the patent, FDA will list the patent, but patent certifications or statements will be governed by the provisions regarding untimely filed patent information at §§ 314.50(i)(4) and (6) and 314.94(a)(12)(vi) and (viii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission avoids special rules for untimely filed patent info; FDA may still list the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and delivery addresses for patent information — filing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent information submitted with the filing of an NDA, amendment, or supplement: The applicant must submit patent information required by paragraphs (c)(1) and (c)(2)(i) of this section and § 314.50(h) or § 314.70(f) on Form FDA 3542a to the Central Document Room, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research ... or to FDA in an electronic format submission that complies with § 314.50(l)(5). Form FDA 3542a should not be submitted to the Orange Book Staff in the Office of Generic Drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form FDA 3542a for submissions at filing; send to Central Document Room or compliant electronic format; do not send to Orange Book Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and delivery addresses for patent information — upon/after approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent information submitted upon and after approval of an NDA or supplement: The applicant must submit patent information required by paragraphs (c)(1) and (c)(2)(ii) of this section on Form FDA 3542 to the Central Document Room ... or to FDA in an electronic format submission that complies with § 314.50(l)(5). Form FDA 3542 should not be submitted to the Orange Book Staff in the Office of Generic Drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form FDA 3542 for post-approval submissions; same address/electronic rules and do not send to Orange Book Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent information will be considered to be submitted to FDA ... as of the earlier of the date the information submitted on Form FDA 3542 is date-stamped by the Central Document Room, or officially received by FDA in an electronic format submission that complies with § 314.50(l)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission date is the earlier of Central Document Room stamping or compliant electronic receipt; important for time-sensitive deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent identification of patent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission of patent information, except information submitted with an original NDA, must bear prominent identification as to its contents, i.e., 'Patent Information,' or, if submitted after approval of an NDA, 'Time Sensitive Patent Information.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label submissions clearly so FDA staff can process correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of submitted patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will publish in the list the patent number and expiration date of each patent that is required to be, and is, submitted to FDA by an applicant, and for each method-of-use patent, the description of the method of use claimed by the patent as required by § 314.53(c)(2)(ii)(P)(3). FDA will publish such patent information upon approval of the NDA, or, if the patent information is submitted by the applicant after approval of an NDA as provided under paragraph (d)(2) of this section, as soon as possible after the submission to the Agency of the patent information. The submitted patent information, and requests to remove a patent or patent information from the list, may be subject to public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent numbers, expiration dates, and method-of-use descriptions will be listed publicly; FOIA requests go to Freedom of Information Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent listing dispute — filing and content for third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person disputes the accuracy or relevance of patent information submitted to the Agency ... that person must first notify the Agency in a written or electronic communication titled '314.53(f) Patent Listing Dispute.' The patent listing dispute communication must include a statement of dispute that describes the specific grounds for disagreement regarding the accuracy or relevance of patent information for FDA to send to the applicable NDA holder. For a dispute regarding the accuracy or relevance of patent information regarding an approved method of using the drug product, this statement of dispute must be only a narrative description (no more than 250 words) of the person's interpretation of the scope of the patent. This statement of dispute must only contain information for which the person consents to disclosure because FDA will send the text of the statement to the applicable NDA holder without review or redaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party disputes must be titled as specified, include specific grounds, and for method-of-use disputes be limited to a 250-word narrative consented for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency communication to NDA holder for drug substance/product disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests ... directed to the accuracy or relevance of submitted patent information regarding a drug substance or drug product claim, the Agency will send the statement of dispute to the applicable NDA holder. The NDA holder must confirm the correctness of the patent information and include the signed verification required by paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(R) of this section or withdraw or amend the patent information in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section within 30 days of the date on which the Agency sends the statement of dispute. Unless the NDA holder withdraws or amends its patent information in response to the patent listing dispute, the Agency will not change the patent information in the Orange Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NDA holder has 30 days to respond with verification or amendment; FDA will not unilaterally change Orange Book without NDA holder action.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA holder response requirements for method-of-use disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests ... directed to the accuracy or relevance of submitted patent information regarding an approved method of using the drug product, FDA will send the statement of dispute to the NDA holder. The NDA holder must confirm the correctness of its description of the approved method of use claimed by the patent that has been included as the 'Use Code' in the Orange Book, or withdraw or amend the patent information in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section, provide a narrative description (no more than 250 words) of the NDA holder's interpretation of the scope of the patent that explains why the existing or amended 'Use Code' describes only the specific approved method of use claimed by the patent for which a claim of patent infringement could reasonably be asserted ... and include the signed verification required by paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(R) of this section within 30 days of the date on which the Agency sends the statement of dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NDA holder must provide a <=250-word narrative interpretation and signed verification; narratives will be sent to the disputant without redaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of NDA holder confirmation or amendment on Orange Book
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NDA holder confirms the correctness of the patent information, provides the narrative description required ... and includes the signed verification ... within 30 days ... the Agency will not change the patent information in the Orange Book. If the NDA holder responds with amended patent information in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) ... provides the narrative description ... and includes the signed verification ... within 30 days ..., FDA will update the Orange Book to reflect the amended patent information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely confirming or timely amending with required narrative and verification determines whether Orange Book entries remain or are updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required patent certifications/statements during listing disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: A 505(b)(2) application or ANDA must contain an appropriate certification or statement for each listed patent, including the disputed patent, during and after the patent listing dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot omit certifications/statements for patents that are under dispute; include appropriate paragraph IV/paragraph II/other certifications as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA posts information on patent listing disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will promptly post information on its Web site regarding whether a patent listing dispute has been submitted for a published description of a patented method of use for a drug product and whether the NDA holder has timely responded to the patent listing dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly visible tracking of disputes and NDA holder responses will be available on FDA's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA holder-initiated corrections/withdrawals when patent no longer meets listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NDA holder determines that a patent or patent claim no longer meets the requirements for listing ... the NDA holder is required to promptly notify FDA to amend the patent information or withdraw the patent or patent information and request that the patent or patent information be removed from the list. If the NDA holder is required by court order to amend patent information or withdraw a patent from the list, it must submit an amendment to its NDA that includes a copy of the order, within 14 days of the date the order was entered ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification is required; court-ordered withdrawals require NDA amendment within 14 days with a copy of the order; FDA will remove patents under defined exclusivity/eligibility conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term restoration reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the term of a listed patent is extended pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 156(e), the NDA holder must submit on Form FDA 3542 a correction to the expiration date of the patent. This correction must be submitted within 30 days of receipt of a certificate of extension ... or documentation of an extension ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report patent term extension promptly on Form FDA 3542 within 30 days of receiving extension documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections/changes to previously submitted patent information must use specified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections or changes to previously submitted patent information, other than withdrawal of a patent and requests to remove a patent from the list, must be submitted on Form FDA 3542 or 3542a, as appropriate, in an amendment or supplement to the NDA. The amendment or supplement to the NDA must bear the identification described in paragraph (d)(6) of this section. We will not accept the corrections or changes unless they are submitted on the appropriate forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct form (3542/3542a) and label the amendment per identification rules; FDA will reject corrections submitted otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and contents for patent withdrawals/requests to remove a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of a patent and requests to remove a patent from the list must be submitted to the same addresses described in paragraph (d)(4)(ii) of this section, except that the withdrawal or request to remove a patent from the list is not required to be submitted on Form FDA 3542 and may be submitted by letter. Withdrawal of a patent and a request to remove a patent from the list must contain the following information: (A) The NDA number to which the request applies; (B) Each product(s) approved in the NDA to which the request applies; and (C) The patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawals/requests may be by letter (not on Form 3542) but must include NDA number, affected products, and patent number; send to designated addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 505(b)(2) application content — archival copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a complete archival copy of the application that contains the following: (i) The information required under § 314.50(a), (b), (c), (d)(1), (d)(3), (e), and (g), except that § 314.50(d)(1)(ii)(c) must contain the proposed or actual master production record, including a description of the equipment, to be used for the manufacture of a commercial lot of the drug product. (ii) The information required under § 314.50(d)(2), (d)(4) (if an anti-infective drug), (d)(5), (d)(6), and (f) as needed to support the safety and effectiveness of the drug product. (iii) Identification of each listed drug for which FDA has made a finding of safety and effectiveness and on which finding the applicant relies ... (iv) If seeking only a new indication and not the listed drug's indications, a certification so stating. (v) Any patent information required under section 505(b)(1) ... (vi) Any patent certification or statement required under section 505(b)(2) ... (vii) If applicant believes change is entitled to exclusivity, information required under § 314.50(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archival copy must be complete and include master production record details; include patent info and certifications as applicable; identify relied-upon listed drugs with full identifying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 505(b)(2) application — review and field copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a review copy that contains the technical sections described in § 314.50(d)(1) ... and the technical sections described in § 314.50(d)(2), (d)(4) through (6), and (f) when needed to support the modification. Each technical section in the review copy is required to be separately bound with a copy of the information required under § 314.50(a), (b), and (c) and a copy of the proposed labeling. The applicant must submit a field copy of the 505(b)(2) application that contains the technical section described in § 314.50(d)(1), a copy of the information required under § 314.50(a) and (c), and certification that the field copy is a true copy of the technical section described in § 314.50(d)(1) contained in the archival and review copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide archival, review, and field copies with specified sections bound; field copy must be certified as true copy of technical section.

rubrics_metrics.name: 505(b)(2) ineligibility when only difference is reduced absorption/availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A 505(b)(2) application may not be submitted under this section for a drug product whose only difference from a listed drug is that: (1) The extent to which its active ingredient(s) is absorbed or otherwise made available to the site of action is less than that of the listed drug; or (2) The rate at which its active ingredient(s) is absorbed or otherwise made available to the site of action is unintentionally less than that of the listed drug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sole difference is lower extent or unintentional lower rate of absorption/availability, 505(b)(2) pathway is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pediatric assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application for a new active ingredient, new indication, new dosage form, new dosing regimen, or new route of administration shall contain data that are adequate to assess the safety and effectiveness of the drug product for the claimed indications in all relevant pediatric subpopulations, and to support dosing and administration for each pediatric subpopulation for which the drug is safe and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where adult and pediatric disease/course are similar, FDA may permit extrapolation from adult studies supplemented with pediatric data (e.g., PK); studies may not be needed in every age group if extrapolation is justified; for products representing meaningful pediatric therapeutic benefit, use appropriate pediatric formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of pediatric assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may, on its own initiative or at the request of an applicant, defer submission of some or all assessments of safety and effectiveness described in paragraph (a) of this section until after approval of the drug product for use in adults. Deferral may be granted if ... the drug is ready for approval in adults before studies in pediatric patients are complete, or pediatric studies should be delayed until additional safety or effectiveness data have been collected. If an applicant requests deferred submission, the request must provide a certification ... a description of the planned or ongoing studies, and evidence that the studies are being or will be conducted with due diligence and at the earliest possible time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to defer must justify grounds, describe studies and show due diligence; FDA may approve adults subject to time-limited requirements to submit pediatric assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers for pediatric assessment — general/full/partial
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant a full or partial waiver of the pediatric assessment requirements on its own initiative or at the request of an applicant. A request for a waiver must provide an adequate justification. Full waiver grounds include certification that (i) product does not represent meaningful therapeutic benefit for pediatric patients and not likely to be used in substantial number of pediatric patients; (ii) necessary studies impossible or highly impractical; or (iii) evidence strongly suggesting product would be ineffective or unsafe in all pediatric age groups. Partial waiver grounds similar but limited to specified pediatric age group including inability to develop formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests must document and certify the ground(s); FDA will grant waivers where reasonable basis exists; waiver consequences (e.g., labeling inclusion if unsafe) are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of meaningful therapeutic benefit for pediatrics
rubrics_metrics.description: A drug will be considered to offer a meaningful therapeutic benefit over existing therapies if FDA estimates that: (i) If approved, the drug would represent a significant improvement in treatment, diagnosis, or prevention of a disease, compared to marketed products adequately labeled for that use in the relevant pediatric population (examples: increased effectiveness, elimination/reduction of treatment-limiting reaction, documented enhancement of compliance, evidence of safety and effectiveness in a new subpopulation); or (ii) The drug is in a class or for an indication for which there is a need for additional therapeutic options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples guide applicants on how to show meaningful benefit; supports decisions on pediatric study requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orphan drug exemption from pediatric requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to any drug for an indication or indications for which orphan designation has been granted under part 316, subpart C, of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drugs with orphan designation for the relevant indication are exempt from these pediatric assessment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ACNU (Additional Condition for Nonprescription Use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional condition for nonprescription use (ACNU) means one or more FDA-approved conditions that an applicant of a nonprescription drug product must implement to ensure consumers' appropriate self-selection or appropriate actual use, or both, of the nonprescription drug product without the supervision of a practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug if an applicant demonstrates and FDA determines that labeling alone is insufficient to ensure appropriate self-selection or appropriate actual use, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACNU is used when labeling alone won't ensure safe/effective nonprescription use; ACNU is an FDA-approved operational condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate application required for nonprescription product with ACNU
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding § 310.200(b) of this chapter, an applicant must submit a separate application for a nonprescription drug product with an ACNU. Initial approval for a nonprescription drug product with an ACNU cannot be obtained through a supplement to an approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACNU-bearing nonprescription products require a new, separate application; cannot convert via supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA content requirements for ACNU products
rubrics_metrics.description: When fulfilling the content and format requirements under § 314.50, an NDA for a nonprescription drug product with an ACNU must include: (i) A statement regarding whether the purpose of the ACNU is to ensure appropriate self-selection or appropriate actual use, or both; (ii) A statement regarding the necessity of the ACNU; (iii) A description of how the ACNU ensures appropriate self-selection or appropriate actual use, or both; (iv) A description of the key elements of the ACNU, including: (A) The additional condition implemented by the applicant to be fulfilled by the consumer to obtain the nonprescription drug product with an ACNU; (B) The labeling specifically associated with the ACNU; and (C) The criteria by which the consumer would successfully fulfill the ACNU, including a description of the specific actions to be taken by a consumer or required responses to be provided by a consumer; (v) Adequate data or other information that demonstrates the necessity of the ACNU; (vi) Adequate data or other information that demonstrates the effect of the ACNU on the appropriate self-selection or appropriate actual use, or both; and (vii) A description of the specific way(s) the ACNU is operationalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit, evidence-backed descriptions of purpose, necessity, key elements, operationalization, labeling, and consumer criteria for ACNU implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA content requirements for ACNU products
rubrics_metrics.description: When fulfilling the content and format requirements under § 314.94, an ANDA for a nonprescription drug product with an ACNU must include: (i) A statement regarding whether the purpose of the ACNU ... which must be the same as the purpose of the ACNU for its reference listed drug (RLD); (ii) Information demonstrating that the key elements of the ACNU are the same as the key elements of the ACNU for its RLD; and (iii) A description of the specific way(s) the ACNU is operationalized. If an applicant believes the ACNU is operationalized in the same way as the RLD, include information demonstrating that the ACNU is operationalized in the same way as the RLD. If a different way to operationalize the proposed ACNU is used, include information to show that this different way ... achieves the same purpose ... and that the differences from the RLD are otherwise acceptable in an ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANDA must demonstrate equivalence of ACNU purpose/elements/operationalization to the RLD or justify acceptable differences with evidence that they achieve same purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU allows simultaneous marketing of prescription and nonprescription products
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACNU constitutes a meaningful difference between a nonprescription drug product and a prescription drug product, such that a prescription drug product and a nonprescription drug product with an ACNU may be simultaneously marketed even if there is not another meaningful difference between the two products that makes the nonprescription drug product safe and effective for use without the supervision of a healthcare practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug (e.g., a different active ingredient, indication, strength, route of administration, dosage form, or patient population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACNU can justify coexistence of prescription and nonprescription versions of essentially the same product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments — applicant may submit amendment to filed but unapproved NDA/supplement/resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA generally assumes that when an original NDA, supplement to an approved NDA, or resubmission of an NDA or supplement is submitted to the Agency for review, the applicant believes that the Agency can approve the NDA, supplement, or resubmission as submitted. However, the applicant may submit an amendment to an NDA, supplement, or resubmission that has been filed under § 314.101 but is not yet approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to pending filings are permitted; see timing rules for impact on review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major amendment timing — extension of initial review cycle (original NDA/efficacy resubmission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a major amendment to an original NDA, efficacy supplement, or resubmission of an NDA or efficacy supplement within 3 months of the end of the initial review cycle constitutes an agreement by the applicant under section 505(c) ... to extend the initial review cycle by 3 months. FDA may instead defer review of the amendment until the subsequent review cycle. The initial review cycle ... may be extended only once due to submission of a major amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting a major amendment near the end of review typically triggers a 3-month extension (only once); FDA may defer instead; applicant will be notified if extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major amendment timing — >3 months before end does not extend cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a major amendment to an original NDA, efficacy supplement, or resubmission ... more than 3 months before the end of the initial review cycle will not extend the cycle. FDA may, at its discretion, review such an amendment during the initial review cycle or defer review until the subsequent review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early major amendments do not automatically extend the review cycle but may be deferred by FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-major amendments do not extend initial review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment to an original NDA, efficacy supplement, or resubmission of an NDA or efficacy supplement that is not a major amendment will not extend the initial review cycle. FDA may, at its discretion, review such an amendment during the initial review cycle or defer review until the subsequent review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor amendments won't extend review time but FDA may choose when to review them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major amendment to manufacturing supplement — 2-month extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a major amendment to a manufacturing supplement within 2 months of the end of the initial review cycle constitutes an agreement by the applicant ... to extend the initial review cycle by 2 months. FDA may instead defer review of the amendment until the subsequent review cycle. The initial review cycle for a manufacturing supplement may be extended only once due to submission of a major amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturing major amendments submitted late can extend the manufacturing supplement review cycle by 2 months (only once); FDA may defer instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to non-efficacy/non-manufacturing supplements do not extend cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment to a supplement other than an efficacy or manufacturing supplement will not extend the initial review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only major efficacy or manufacturing amendments near the end of cycle have automatic extension effects; other supplement amendments do not.
